findings.title: generateSkill duplicates the agent loop's compare/check/write logic instead of sharing a helper
findings.detail: run()'s per-agent loop (lines 66-78: read dst, bytes.Equal skip, `check` → print "stale:" + count, else write() + print "wrote") is the same four-branch shape newly written again in generateSkill (lines 117-127) for the skill file. Both were touched/added by this wave's task-3. A small `writeOrReport(dst, out, check, stdout, stderr) (stale int, err error)` would serve both call sites; instead the diff reimplements the pattern rather than factoring it, which is exactly the 'duplicated helper' this lens looks for — and it is the same file, so a future edit to one copy (e.g. the stale-message wording) can silently drift from the other.

findings.title: Missing-version-field error reads differently from the CLI's own phrasing for the same condition
findings.detail: hostgen's manifestVersion renders a missing/empty "version" field as `fmt.Errorf("%s: no \"version\" field", path)` (internal/tools/hostgen/main.go:148), while internal/cli/cmd_version.go:139 renders the identical condition — an empty version in the same .claude-plugin/plugin.json — as `"plugin manifest " + path + " has no version field"`. Same fact, two different sentence shapes and quoting conventions for the one JSON field this wave's task-3 cares about (§2.3's version handshake).

findings.title: Slice-floor-to-1 rule hand-duplicated between timingKeyOf and closeKeyOf
findings.detail: timingKeyOf (line 309: `max(int(sl), 1)`) and the new closeKeyOf (line 317: `max(c.Slice, 1)`) encode the same 'floor a missing/zero slice to 1' rule inline in two places rather than through one named helper (e.g. `floorSlice(n int) int`). closeKeyOf's own doc comment even says it floors 'the way [timingKeyOf] floors', which is a hint the two could share one function instead of restating the rule.

findings.title: manifestVersion names a function here but a struct/type for the same concept elsewhere in the codebase
findings.detail: internal/tools/hostgen/main.go:136 introduces `func manifestVersion(path string) (string, error)`, and internal/prompt/copilot_test.go:100 (this same wave) introduces a same-named test helper function. internal/cli/cmd_version.go:88 already has `type manifestVersion struct { Version string }` for the identical concept (the plugin manifest's version field). Different packages so it compiles, but the same identifier names a type in one place and a function in two others for what the brief itself treats as one recurring concept (spec §2.3's handshake version).
